question: Does the supported xy ridge stay under 20 px on both coordinates when each test episode counts once, on seeds 0 and 1?
claim: The frozen Ridge(alpha=1) from stored float32 z to (x, y), scored as the unweighted mean of per-episode mean absolute errors, is below 20 px on both coordinates for both seed 0 and seed 1, and each of those four numbers is strictly below the train-mean constant predictor scored the same way.
falsifier: Kill if any of the four episode-level MAEs is at least 40 px. Any other computed result that misses the support line weakens. Inconclusive only if the MAE cannot be computed.
assumptions: The ridge, the float32 latent, and seeds 0 and 1 are the fits already in ledger rows 002 and 003
An episode score is the mean absolute error of its frames, then the mean of those episode scores
Rotation test episodes have 4 frames and random-only test episodes have 1 frame
The constant predictor is the training-frame mean, not an episode mean
degenerate_check: Episode weighting can clear 20 px when the constant predictor already does, or when the frame-level fit is recomputed on a different split. Support requires the frame-level ledger numbers to reproduce and each episode-level MAE to beat its constant predictor.

next_action.deepen: Same fits and seeds. Score the fraction of test episodes whose per-coordinate episode-mean absolute error is under 15 px on both coordinates. Write that falsifier before the rescore. Do not add a model class. Do not start B6 inside that rescore.
next_action.pivot: The episode-level <20 px claim is withdrawn. Do not retune the ridge. Ledger rows 002 and 003 stay. The next new claim is B6 on the Xeon.
next_action.kill: Archive the episode-level xy claim. Ledger rows 002 and 003 stay. The next cycle may frame B6 only, on the Xeon.
next_action.escalate: Stop. Do not rent a GPU.
